shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, reducing variety and utility. I value having at least one of each good more than an extra B.
This trade would give me 2A, 0B, 1C, creating imbalance and losing variety value. Since I value variety, going to 0 of B is worse than staying balanced at 1-1-1.
Trading away my only B for more A would leave me with zero B, hurting the variety balance I value across A, B, and C.
Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1), so trading away C for B would just shift the imbalance to C without net benefit, since both goods are equally scarce for me.

Trading away B for C would just flip my inventory imbalance (1,0,2) instead of improving variety; I currently have equal 1-1-1 which is already balanced, so this trade would reduce my utility by creating imbalance.
Giving up my only B to get more C would leave me with none of B, reducing variety which I value. Better to seek a more balanced trade.
This trade would give me 2B and 0A, creating imbalance (A:0, B:2, C:1), which reduces variety value compared to my current even 1-1-1 split. Not beneficial.
Trading away my only B for a second A would unbalance my equal 1-1-1 holdings, reducing variety value. I prefer to keep balanced inventory unless offered something that increases diversity.
Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 3A,0B,1C, drastically reducing variety which I value highly. Current balanced bundle is better.

I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C (1 each). Trading away C for B would just shift the imbalance to C=0, B=2, which doesn't improve variety - it's a lateral move that reduces my diversity rather than increasing it.
Trading B for C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety instead of improving it. Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1), so this trade would decrease my utility.
This would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a worse variety imbalance. I prefer to keep a more even distribution across A, B, and C rather than trade away my only B for more C.
This would give me 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and leaving me with an empty category, which decreases my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.
This would just swap one unit for another, giving me 2A and 0B, reducing variety instead of improving balance. I prefer to keep an even distribution across A, B, and C.
Giving up my only B to end with zero B and 3 A would hurt variety; I'd rather keep a balanced inventory.
Trading 1C for 1B would leave me with 2B and 0C, moving from an even 1-1-1 bundle to an unbalanced one, decreasing variety value.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C (1 each), so trading away B for C would just shift the imbalance to B=0, C=2 instead of improving variety. This trade doesn't increase my utility.
Giving up my only B would leave me with none of that good, reducing variety which I value. Better to keep a balanced inventory.
Trading A(2) for B gives me A:1,B:2,C:0, improving variety balance since I currently have surplus A and scarce B.
I already have 2 A and only 1 B and 0 C. Trading away my only B for more A would worsen my variety balance, moving to 3A/0B/0C which is less diverse. I'd rather keep or gain B/C instead.
Giving up all my A for just 1 more B would leave me with 0 A and 0 C, badly hurting variety. Not favorable.
This would leave me with 4A, 0B, 0C, worsening variety drastically. I'd rather keep B and seek C instead.
Trading away my only B for C just swaps which good I'm missing, without improving variety or balance of my bundle.

Trading away my single B for 2C diversifies my inventory from (2,1,0) to (2,0,2). Since marginal value decreases with quantity, gaining two units of a good I have none of outweighs losing my sole B, giving a net utility gain due to variety preference.
I currently have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading 1A for 1B gives me A:1, B:1, C:1, a perfectly balanced bundle which maximizes my variety-preferring utility.

Giving 2A for only 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 1C - too extreme a swing, losing all variety in A. I'd rather get 1B for 1A to balance my inventory (2A,0B,1C -> 1A,1B,1C) which is more balanced and valuable to me.

I currently have 0 B and 1 C, so giving up my only C would leave me with 2A,1B,0C - just shifting the imbalance rather than improving variety. I'd prefer to keep C and acquire B through a trade that doesn't cost me my only unit of another scarce good.
Current inventory A:2,B:0,C:2. Trading 1A for 1B gives A:1,B:1,C:2 - improves variety balance since B was at zero, increasing overall utility despite reducing A.
Giving up both A would leave me with none, hurting variety. I'd prefer a trade of 1 A for 1 B instead.
I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading away a redundant C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my inventory to A:2, B:1, C:1.

Current bundle (2A,0B,2C) already has variety across A and C; trading away all my C for B just shifts the zero from B to C without improving diversity, slightly lowering my diminishing-returns utility (sqrt(2)+sqrt(2)=2.83 vs sqrt(2)+sqrt(1)=2.41). Better to hold or negotiate a smaller C-for-B trade.

Trading away my only A would leave me with zero A while still having zero B before the trade- it just shifts which good I'm missing, not a net improvement. I'd rather find a trade that improves variety without zeroing out another good.
